title: Dominant Banner
statement:
DOMINANT BANNER

N guards stand in a line numbered 1 to N. Initially, guard i holds clan banner A_i. You process Q events of two types:
- 1 P X: guard P replaces their banner with banner X.
- 2 L R: among guards L, L+1, ..., R, find the clan banner held by STRICTLY MORE than (R - L + 1) / 2 guards, or report 0 if no such banner exists.

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains A_1 ... A_N.
Each of the next Q lines describes an event in one of the two formats above. At least one event is of type 2.

Output
For each event of type 2, print the strictly dominant banner number, or 0 if none exists, on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
1 <= A_i, X <= N
1 <= P <= N
1 <= L <= R <= N

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
6 5
2 1 2 2 3 1
2 1 4
2 2 6
1 5 2
2 2 6
2 5 6

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
2
0
2
0

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Mountain Couriers
statement:
MOUNTAIN COURIERS

A mountain province has N villages numbered 1 to N connected by M bidirectional roads. Road i connects villages U_i and V_i and crosses a pass of altitude W_i. The road network is connected (multiple roads may connect the same pair of villages).

You are asked Q courier queries. Each query specifies a start village A and a destination village B: find the minimum oxygen rating R such that a courier can travel from A to B using only roads with altitude at most R (if A = B, the answer is 0).

Input
The first line contains N, M, and Q.
Each of the next M lines contains U_i, V_i, and W_i.
Each of the next Q lines contains A and B.

Output
For each query print the minimum required altitude rating on its own line.

Constraints
2 <= N <= 200000
N - 1 <= M <= 200000
1 <= Q <= 200000
1 <= U_i, V_i <= N, U_i != V_i
1 <= W_i <= 10^9

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
4 5 3
1 2 5
2 3 8
1 3 6
3 4 4
2 4 9
1 4
2 4
3 3

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
6
6
0

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: River Couriers
statement:
RIVER COURIERS

Along a river are N docks numbered 1 to N from upstream to downstream. A message starts at dock 1 (with initial cost 0) and must reach dock N by a sequence of boat hops that always move strictly downstream (from some dock j to a dock i > j).

Each dock i has three parameters: fuel rate A_i, current factor D_i, and harbour fee F_i. Sending a boat directly from dock j to dock i (j < i) costs A_j * D_i + F_i.

For every dock i = 2, 3, ..., N, find the minimum total cost for the message to reach dock i starting from dock 1.

Input
The first line contains N.
The second line contains A_1 ... A_N.
The third line contains D_1 ... D_N.
The fourth line contains F_1 ... F_N.

Output
Print N - 1 lines: on the k-th line print the minimum total cost to reach dock k + 1.

Constraints
2 <= N <= 200000
1 <= A_i, D_i <= 10^6
0 <= F_i <= 10^11

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
4
5 2 8 1
3 6 4 10
10 5 7 2

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
35
27
52

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Mirror Scroll
statement:
MIRROR SCROLL

An ancient scroll consists of N lowercase English letters indexed 1 to N. Process Q operations of two types:
- 1 P C: replace the character at position P with lowercase letter C.
- 2 L R: check whether the substring from position L to position R (inclusive) reads the same forwards and backwards (is a palindrome).

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains the initial string of length N.
Each of the next Q lines describes an operation in one of the two formats above. At least one operation is of type 2.

Output
For each operation of type 2, print YES if the substring is a palindrome, or NO otherwise.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
1 <= P <= N
1 <= L <= R <= N
All characters are lowercase English letters ('a'-'z').

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
7 5
abacaba
2 1 7
2 2 5
1 4 z
2 1 7
1 2 c

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
YES
NO
YES

Sample input 2 (file sample_2.in)
5 3
abcba
2 1 5
1 2 x
2 1 5

Sample output 2 (file sample_2.out)
YES
NO

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Guard Rotations
statement:
GUARD ROTATIONS

A border watch runs for K integer hours numbered 1 to K. There are M available guard shifts; shift i covers every integer hour from L_i to R_i inclusive.

You are given Q inspection queries. Query j specifies A and B (1 <= A <= B <= K): find the minimum number of shifts needed so that every integer hour from A to B inclusive is covered by at least one chosen shift, or print -1 if it is impossible.

Input
The first line contains K, M, and Q.
Each of the next M lines contains L_i and R_i.
Each of the next Q lines contains A and B.

Output
For each query print the minimum number of shifts (or -1) on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= K, M, Q <= 200000
1 <= L_i <= R_i <= K
1 <= A <= B <= K

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
10 5 4
1 4
3 7
6 9
9 10
2 5
1 10
2 7
5 8
8 10

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
4
2
2
2

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Stepped Terraces
statement:
STEPPED TERRACES

A hillside has N garden terraces numbered 1 to N, where terrace i currently has integer elevation A_i. Raising or lowering any terrace by 1 metre costs 1 unit of labour.

Choose new integer elevations B_1, B_2, ..., B_N (negative or zero integer elevations are allowed) such that B_1 < B_2 < ... < B_N (strictly increasing), minimizing the total labour sum_{i=1..N} |A_i - B_i|.

Input
The first line contains N.
The second line contains A_1 ... A_N.

Output
Print a single integer: the minimum total labour required.

Constraints
1 <= N <= 200000
1 <= A_i <= 10^9

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
5
5 4 3 2 1

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
12

Sample input 2 (file sample_2.in)
4
2 2 2 2

Sample output 2 (file sample_2.out)
4

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Timber Quotas
statement:
TIMBER QUOTAS

A kingdom has N provinces numbered 1 to N and M timber yards arranged in a row numbered 1 to M. Yard j belongs to province O_j. Province i needs to accumulate at least R_i logs in total across all timber yards it owns.

Over Q days (numbered 1 to Q), day t delivers W_t logs to EVERY yard j with L_t <= j <= R_t. For each province i = 1, 2, ..., N, find the earliest day t after which province i has accumulated at least R_i logs in total, or print -1 if its quota is still unmet after all Q days.

Input
The first line contains N, M, and Q.
The second line contains O_1 ... O_M.
The third line contains R_1 ... R_N.
Each of the next Q lines contains L_t, R_t, and W_t.

Output
Print N lines: on line i print the earliest day province i meets its quota, or -1 if never.

Constraints
1 <= N, M, Q <= 150000
1 <= O_j <= N
1 <= R_i <= 10^12
1 <= L_t <= R_t <= M
1 <= W_t <= 10^7

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
3 5 4
1 2 1 3 2
10 15 8
1 3 4
2 5 6
1 5 5
4 4 10

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
2
2
3

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Sunken Courtyard
statement:
SUNKEN COURTYARD

A courtyard is a grid of H rows and W columns (1-indexed from (1, 1) at top-left to (H, W) at bottom-right). K distinct cells other than (1, 1) and (H, W) are flooded and cannot be entered.

In each step you may move one cell down ((r, c) -> (r + 1, c)) or one cell right ((r, c) -> (r, c + 1)). Count the number of valid paths from (1, 1) to (H, W) that never step onto a flooded cell, modulo 10^9 + 7.

Input
The first line contains H, W, and K.
Each of the next K lines contains R_i and C_i, the coordinates of a flooded cell.

Output
Print a single integer: the number of valid paths modulo 10^9 + 7.

Constraints
2 <= H, W <= 200000
0 <= K <= 2500
1 <= R_i <= H, 1 <= C_i <= W
All flooded cells are distinct and neither (1, 1) nor (H, W) is flooded.

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
3 4 2
2 2
2 3

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
2

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Citadel Enclosure
statement:
CITADEL ENCLOSURE

A central citadel stands at the origin (0, 0). Around it stand N watchtowers; watchtower i is at integer coordinates (X_i, Y_i). No watchtower stands at (0, 0), and no line through (0, 0) passes through two or more watchtowers.

Count how many unordered triples of distinct watchtowers {i, j, k} form a triangle that strictly encloses the origin (0, 0).

Input
The first line contains N.
Each of the next N lines contains X_i and Y_i.

Output
Print a single integer: the number of enclosing triangles.

Constraints
3 <= N <= 180000
-10^9 <= X_i, Y_i <= 10^9
No line through (0, 0) contains two or more watchtowers.

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
4
1 1
-2 1
0 -3
2 1

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
2

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Signal Modulators
statement:
SIGNAL MODULATORS

An array of N signal amplifiers is numbered 1 to N, where amplifier i initially outputs power A_i. Process Q operations of three types:
- 1 L R M: for every i from L to R, replace A_i with (A_i mod M).
- 2 P X: set A_P to X.
- 3 L R: report the sum A_L + A_{L+1} + ... + A_R.

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains A_1 ... A_N.
Each of the next Q lines describes an operation in one of the three formats above. At least one operation is of type 3.

Output
For each operation of type 3, print the range sum on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 180000
0 <= A_i, X <= 10^9
1 <= M <= 10^9
1 <= P <= N
1 <= L <= R <= N

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
5 5
10 7 15 4 9
3 1 5
1 2 4 6
3 1 5
2 3 20
3 2 5

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
45
27
34

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Signal Windows
statement:
SIGNAL WINDOWS

A radio telescope records N consecutive signal measurements A_1, A_2, ..., A_N (which may be positive, zero, or negative).

You may choose AT MOST K pairwise non-overlapping contiguous windows, where EVERY chosen window has exact length L. That is, you choose m (0 <= m <= K) starting indices s_1, s_2, ..., s_m such that:
- 1 <= s_1,
- s_j + L <= s_{j+1} for all 1 <= j < m, and
- s_m + L - 1 <= N.

Find the maximum possible total sum of all measurements inside your chosen windows (choosing m = 0 windows gives a sum of 0).

Input
The first line contains N, K, and L.
The second line contains A_1 ... A_N.

Output
Print the maximum achievable total sum.

Constraints
1 <= L <= N <= 200000
1 <= K <= 60000
-10^6 <= A_i <= 10^6

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
8 2 3
2 -1 4 3 -2 5 1 -3

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
11

Sample input 2 (file sample_2.in)
5 3 2
-4 -2 -5 -1 -3

Sample output 2 (file sample_2.out)
0

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Balanced Stones
statement:
BALANCED STONES

An alchemist has N stones with positive integer weights W_1, W_2, ..., W_N, whose total weight S = W_1 + W_2 + ... + W_N is at most 240000.

For each target weight x from 1 to S:
- Let f(x) be the MINIMUM number of stones needed to form a subset of total weight exactly x, or 0 if no subset of stones sums to x.

Compute two values:
1. K, the number of target weights x in [1, S] that CAN be formed.
2. T = f(1) + f(2) + ... + f(S), the sum of minimum stone counts across all achievable positive target weights.

Input
The first line contains N.
The second line contains W_1 ... W_N.

Output
Print two space-separated integers: K and T.

Constraints
1 <= N <= 200000
1 <= W_i <= 240000
W_1 + W_2 + ... + W_N <= 240000

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
5
1 1 2 2 5

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
11 26

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Common Borders
statement:
COMMON BORDERS

A proper border of a non-empty string T is a string B with 0 <= |B| < |T| that occurs BOTH as a prefix of T and as a suffix of T (the empty string of length 0 is always a proper border).

You are given a string S of length N (1-indexed) and Q queries. Each query specifies two prefix lengths P and R (1 <= P, R <= N): find the maximum length of a string that is simultaneously a proper border of S[1..P] AND a proper border of S[1..R].

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains S.
Each of the next Q lines contains P and R.

Output
For each query print the maximum common proper border length on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 200000
S consists of lowercase English letters ('a'-'z')
1 <= P, R <= N

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
7 4
abababa
3 5
5 5
1 7
4 6

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
1
3
0
2

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Substring Frequencies
statement:
SUBSTRING FREQUENCIES

You are given a string S of length N and Q queries. Each query specifies two integers A and B (1 <= A <= B <= N): count how many DISTINCT non-empty substrings T of S occur in S at least A times and at most B times (overlapping occurrences count; for example, "aba" occurs twice in "ababa").

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
The second line contains S.
Each of the next Q lines contains A and B.

Output
For each query print the number of distinct substrings whose occurrence count lies in [A, B] on its own line.

Constraints
1 <= N, Q <= 160000
S consists of lowercase English letters ('a'-'z')
1 <= A <= B <= N

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
5 4
ababa
1 5
2 2
3 5
1 1

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
9
4
1
4

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Censored Chronicle
statement:
CENSORED CHRONICLE

A royal scribe copies a text T from left to right into an initially empty scroll R, checking a list of K forbidden words P_1, P_2, ..., P_K after each character:
1. Append the next character of T to the end of R.
2. If one or more forbidden words now appear as a suffix of R, immediately erase the LONGEST such forbidden word from the end of R.

After all characters of T have been processed, print the final contents of the scroll R, or print EMPTY if R has length 0.

Input
The first line contains the text T.
The second line contains K.
Each of the next K lines contains a forbidden word P_i.

Output
Print the final string R, or EMPTY if R is empty.

Constraints
1 <= |T| <= 200000
1 <= K <= 100000
1 <= |P_i|, and |P_1| + |P_2| + ... + |P_K| <= 200000
T and all P_i consist of lowercase English letters ('a'-'z')

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
abxabyabz
2
aby
ababz

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
abxabz

Sample input 2 (file sample_2.in)
aabb
1
ab

Sample output 2 (file sample_2.out)
EMPTY

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.
samples:

2
aby
ababz
abxabz
aabb
1
ab

title: Floor Harmonics
statement:
FLOOR HARMONICS

You are given N positive integers A_1, A_2, ..., A_N. Compute the sum over ALL ordered pairs (i, j) with 1 <= i <= N and 1 <= j <= N of floor(A_i / A_j).

Input
The first line contains N.
The second line contains A_1 ... A_N.

Output
Print a single integer: the value of sum_{i=1..N} sum_{j=1..N} floor(A_i / A_j).

Constraints
1 <= N <= 200000
1 <= A_i <= 500000

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
4
2 5 7 3

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
14

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Skewer Combinations
statement:
SKEWER COMBINATIONS

A festival kitchen has N ingredient packs. Pack i contains A_i pieces of meat and B_i pieces of vegetables.

When two distinct packs i and j (1 <= i < j <= N) are combined onto a single skewer, the number of distinct ways to arrange all (A_i + A_j) indistinguishable meat pieces and (B_i + B_j) indistinguishable vegetable pieces in a row is the binomial coefficient:
C(A_i + A_j + B_i + B_j, A_i + A_j).

Compute the sum of C(A_i + A_j + B_i + B_j, A_i + A_j) over all N * (N - 1) / 2 pairs 1 <= i < j <= N, modulo 10^9 + 7.

Input
The first line contains N.
Each of the next N lines contains two integers A_i and B_i.

Output
Print the total sum modulo 10^9 + 7.

Constraints
2 <= N <= 200000
1 <= A_i, B_i <= 2000

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
3
1 1
1 2
2 1

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
40

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Skyline Shadows
statement:
SKYLINE SHADOWS

On a flat plain, N rectangular solar canopies cast shadows on the ground. Canopy i covers the axis-aligned rectangle [X_{1,i}, X_{2,i}] x [Y_{1,i}, Y_{2,i}] (with X_{1,i} < X_{2,i} and Y_{1,i} < Y_{2,i}). Canopies may overlap arbitrarily.

Compute the exact total area of the union of all N rectangles.

Input
The first line contains N.
Each of the next N lines contains four integers X_{1,i}, Y_{1,i}, X_{2,i}, and Y_{2,i}.

Output
Print a single integer: the exact area of the union of the N rectangles.

Constraints
1 <= N <= 150000
0 <= X_{1,i} < X_{2,i} <= 10^9
0 <= Y_{1,i} < Y_{2,i} <= 10^9

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
3
1 1 5 4
3 2 7 6
6 1 8 3

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
27

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Consecutive Blocks
statement:
CONSECUTIVE BLOCKS

You are given a permutation P_1, P_2, ..., P_N of the integers {1, 2, ..., N}.

A contiguous subarray [L, R] (1 <= L <= R <= N) is called a CONSECUTIVE BLOCK if sorting the elements P_L, P_{L+1}, ..., P_R produces a sequence of consecutive integers (equivalently, max(P_L..P_R) - min(P_L..P_R) = R - L).

Count the total number of consecutive blocks [L, R].

Input
The first line contains N.
The second line contains P_1 ... P_N.

Output
Print a single integer: the number of pairs (L, R) with 1 <= L <= R <= N that form a consecutive block.

Constraints
1 <= N <= 200000
P_1 ... P_N is a permutation of {1, 2, ..., N}

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
5
3 2 5 4 1

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
9

Sample input 2 (file sample_2.in)
4
2 4 1 3

Sample output 2 (file sample_2.out)
5

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Platform Dispatch
statement:
PLATFORM DISPATCH

A central rail station has K parallel platforms and receives N train reservation requests. Train i requires a single platform from arrival time L_i to departure time R_i (with L_i < R_i).

A single platform cannot serve two overlapping trains, except back-to-back: if one train departs at time R_i and another arrives at time L_j >= R_i, they MAY share the same platform. Each accepted train must stay on one platform for its entire stay, and you may reject any subset of requests.

Find the maximum number of trains that can be accommodated across the K platforms.

Input
The first line contains N and K.
Each of the next N lines contains L_i and R_i.

Output
Print a single integer: the maximum number of trains that can be scheduled.

Constraints
1 <= K <= N <= 200000
0 <= L_i < R_i <= 10^9

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
5 2
1 5
6 8
2 9
1 10
8 11

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
4

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Tinted Highways
statement:
TINTED HIGHWAYS

A kingdom has N cities numbered 1 to N connected by N - 1 bidirectional roads forming a tree. Road i connects U_i and V_i, is painted color C_i (1 <= C_i <= N - 1), and has base length W_i.

Answer Q independent hypothetical queries. Each query gives four integers A, B, K, and X: if EVERY road of color K had its length temporarily changed to X (while roads of all other colors keep their base lengths), what would be the total length of the unique simple path between city A and city B?

Input
The first line contains N and Q.
Each of the next N - 1 lines contains four integers U_i, V_i, C_i, and W_i.
Each of the next Q lines contains four integers A, B, K, and X.

Output
For each query print the hypothetical path length between A and B on its own line.

Constraints
2 <= N <= 180000
1 <= Q <= 180000
1 <= U_i, V_i, A, B <= N
1 <= C_i, K <= N - 1
0 <= W_i, X <= 10^7

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
5 3
1 2 1 10
2 3 2 20
2 4 1 30
4 5 3 40
1 5 1 5
3 5 2 100
1 4 3 999

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
50
170
40

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.

title: Segmented Convoys
statement:
SEGMENTED CONVOYS

A logistics fleet must divide a sequence of N crates with positive weights A_1, A_2, ..., A_N (preserving their order) into EXACTLY K non-empty contiguous convoys.

If convoy t carries crates L_t, L_t + 1, ..., R_t with total weight S_t = A_{L_t} + ... + A_{R_t}, road wear imposes a quadratic surcharge of (S_t)^2.

Find the minimum possible total surcharge sum_{t=1..K} (S_t)^2 across all valid partitions into K non-empty contiguous convoys.

Input
The first line contains N and K.
The second line contains A_1 ... A_N.

Output
Print a single integer: the minimum possible sum of squared convoy weights.

Constraints
1 <= K <= N <= 150000
1 <= A_i <= 2000

Sample input 1 (file sample_1.in)
6 3
3 1 4 1 5 2

Sample output 1 (file sample_1.out)
90

Sample input 2 (file sample_2.in)
4 4
7 2 5 3

Sample output 2 (file sample_2.out)
87

Limits: 2 seconds and 1024 MiB of memory per test.
